findings.title: Moovember 2026 | Feature & Security Update: Mailbox Groups, imapsync Rework & SOGo 5.12.13
findings.summary_md: Mailcow's vendor blog published the 2026-11 release on 5 November 2026 with an important security update and a recommendation to update as soon as possible. The post says the release fixes a remote code execution vulnerability exploitable by authenticated admins and domain admins, with details promised for early the following week. The stated workaround until updating is to limit access to admin and domain admin accounts. The release also ships SOGo 5.12.13, an upstream security release, and a 64 MB request body limit for the UI and API.

findings.title: Release 2026-11: Moovember 2026 Feature & Security Update
findings.summary_md: The GitHub release record for tag 2026-11, published 5 November 2026 at 10:23 UTC, carries the same security warning: the release fixes an RCE exploitable by authenticated admins and domain admins, and details on the fixed issues will be published early the next week. The listed workaround is to limit access to admin and domain admin accounts. The notes list several security fixes in mailcow, SOGo 5.12.13, and a 64 MB request body limit for the UI and API.

findings.title: GHSA-jgr3-fv33-x43c: Domain admin stored SSTI in domain_wide_footer leads to RCE in the shared rspamd container (cross-tenant)
findings.summary_md: GitHub advisory GHSA-jgr3-fv33-x43c, published 10 November 2026, rates a stored server-side template injection in the mailcow domain-wide footer at CVSS 9.1 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H). A domain administrator stores footer HTML that rspamd's jinja and lupa engine renders on authenticated outbound mail, and a macro default value reaches Lua os.execute for code execution in the shared rspamd container. The advisory states the impact spans all hosted domains, covering mail read, modification and injection plus platform-wide filtering disable, and documents a post-exploitation path to container lifecycle actions through the internal MC_CHANNEL and dockerapi plane. No CVE ID is assigned yet.

findings.title: GHSA-rpvp-3pw9-3vcw: Failed ActiveSync/DAV/autodiscover logins are never banned, and passwordless autodiscover reveals which mailboxes exist
findings.summary_md: GitHub advisory GHSA-rpvp-3pw9-3vcw, published 10 November 2026, covers two issues found in release 2026-09a. Failed ActiveSync, CalDAV/CardDAV and autodiscover logins were reported to netfilter with 127.0.0.1 as the client address and were never counted or banned, while passwordless autodiscover disclosed which mailboxes exist and their owners' display names. The advisory rates the combined issue 7.4 and says an unauthenticated attacker could run unlimited password guessing against every mailbox with EAS or DAV access, which is enabled by default. Fixed in 2026-11.

findings.title: GHSA-vv9q-w88c-j8h7: Cross-Tenant Quarantine Metadata Disclosure via Unescaped Domain Regex
findings.summary_md: GitHub advisory GHSA-vv9q-w88c-j8h7, published 10 November 2026, describes a cross-tenant quarantine metadata disclosure rated 3.1. The quarantine list for domain administrators filtered recipients with an unescaped SQL regular expression, so dots in a domain name matched any character and a domain administrator of h.des.test could see entries for user@hades.test. The advisory credits researcher Mohammad Nikouei and says the issue requires two domains whose names collide in this way. Fixed in 2026-11.

findings.title: GHSA-xvvm-8287-x8f9: TOTP 2FA brute-force with a known password due to missing rate limiting on TFA verification
findings.summary_md: GitHub advisory GHSA-xvvm-8287-x8f9, published 10 November 2026, rates a TOTP 2FA brute-force flaw at 6.8. Failed second-factor checks had no rate limiting, attempt counting or lockout, so an attacker who knew a user's password could try TOTP codes indefinitely across admin, domain admin and mailbox roles. Fixed in 2026-11 with per-account counting, a lock after 10 failures within 15 minutes, and netfilter reporting for failed second factors.

findings.title: GHSA-6v9c-2j28-pfhv: Manage app passwords permission only enforced in the web interface
findings.summary_md: GitHub advisory GHSA-6v9c-2j28-pfhv, published 10 November 2026, rates an authorization gap at 4.3. The per-mailbox ACL for managing app passwords was enforced only in the web interface, so a mailbox user whose administrator had removed the permission could still create, edit and delete app passwords through the JSON API using a normal session. Fixed in 2026-11 by checking the app_passwds permission server-side.
